---
name: airline-route-profitability-review
description: Use for route profitability, network economics, PRASM/CASM, and budget performance reviews.
---

1. Resolve period and comparison.
2. Use route-month P&L and verify coverage.
3. Report revenue, operating cost, income and ratio-of-sums margin, load factors, RASM and CASM as relevant.
4. Compare actuals with budget and prior period using matched coverage.
5. Rank material gaps; distinguish size from rate.
6. Explain source units and limitations; do not claim demand forecasts or causal drivers.

---
name: airline-operational-reliability-review
description: Use for punctuality, cancellations, delays, carrier, fleet, or airport reliability reviews.
---

1. Resolve travel period.
2. Use flight-grain view.
3. Count scheduled flights, cancellations and diversions separately.
4. Calculate arrival OTP only among non-cancelled, non-diverted flights.
5. Segment by route, carrier, airport or fleet with volumes.
6. Treat weather and inbound delay as associations; validate joins at airport-day grain.
7. Summarize observations and investigation priorities.

---
name: airline-customer-experience-review
description: Use for NPS, satisfaction, service cases, baggage claims, or customer experience diagnosis.
---

1. State event-date basis for each subject.
2. Compute survey NPS from valid responses, with sample size.
3. Analyze service cases and baggage claims independently; never multiply facts through detail joins.
4. Keep money and miles compensation separate.
5. Compare cohorts with adequate samples and label associations.
6. Summarize evidence, limitations and follow-up questions.

---
name: airline-loyalty-and-co-brand-review
description: Use for loyalty activity, miles balances, card accounts or partner remuneration analysis.
---

1. Resolve month and historical tier basis.
2. Treat balances, YTD measures and active-account counts as snapshots.
3. Separate customer-month, account-month and product-month facts.
4. Distinguish cardholder spend from airline revenue.
5. Calculate remuneration less program cost for net remuneration.
6. Report activity and balances separately; do not assert retention effects.

---
name: airline-commercial-performance-review
description: Use for ticket sales, channels, cabins, fare products, ancillaries and commercial mix analysis.
---

1. Resolve booking versus travel versus purchase period.
2. Use ticket segment for ticket measures and ancillary sales for net ancillary transactions.
3. State boarded/award/revenue eligibility rules rather than guessing them.
4. Use independent aggregates when comparing facts.
5. Compare revenue, volume, mix and distribution cost.
6. Do not invent named-account commitments or confuse total fare with recognized passenger revenue.

---
name: airline-technical-answer-validation
description: Use when validating an airline answer, troubleshooting SQL, or preparing a workshop demonstration.
---

1. Inspect selected sources and native grains.
2. Check date basis, coverage and filters.
3. Check joins, duplicate keys, row counts and fanout.
4. Recompute ratios from sums and snapshots at a single date.
5. Execute reference SQL and compare results using stated tolerances.
6. Record failures and corrections.
7. Keep holdout questions separate from reviewed training examples; do not mark unexecuted SQL as validated.
